sources.title: Bühler and Salamon, Functional Analysis, 2017
sources.locator: Selected named results in §§3.1.1–3.1.4 pp118–131, and Exercises 3.60–3.62 pp161–162. Exact harvested locators below.

contents.name: Lemma 3.6: topology induced by linear functionals
contents.support: Finite evaluation neighborhoods and local convexity; separating family gives Hausdorffness.

contents.name: Weak and weak-star topology examples
contents.support: Use X* for weak and evaluation vectors for weak-star.

contents.name: Lemma 3.13: finite-kernel factorization
contents.support: Finite-dimensional factorization, not unrestricted algebraic duality.

contents.name: Lemma 3.14 and Theorem 3.12: continuous dual of an induced topology
contents.support: Finite linear combinations of generating functionals.

contents.name: Lemma 3.15: convex closedness
contents.support: Closed convex sets are precisely intersections of continuous half-spaces.

contents.name: Lemma 3.16: weakly continuous linear functionals
contents.support: Continuous dual identification.

contents.name: Lemma 3.17: annihilator closure
contents.support: Closed kernels.

contents.name: Lemma 3.18: linear-subspace closure and annihilators
contents.support: Already homed on the published duality predecessor.

contents.name: Lemma 3.19: closed convex hull
contents.support: Closure version follows using half-spaces.

contents.name: Lemma 3.20: Mazur convex combinations
contents.support: Underlying closed-convex-set separation already proved; sequence-tail formulation is an application.

contents.name: Lemma 3.21: weak closure of the sphere
contents.support: Infinite-dimensional common-kernel line argument.

contents.name: Corollary 3.25: weak-star continuous dual
contents.support: Evaluation at one vector.

contents.name: Corollary 3.26: weak-star closure of a subspace
contents.support: Published predecessor keeps canonical identity.

contents.name: Corollary 3.27: weak-star convex separation
contents.support: Finite evaluation separation supports the following pair; no use of later compactness.

contents.name: Corollary 3.29: Goldstine density
contents.support: Dense bidual embedding; closed-ball formulation also checked by Teschl 5.13.

contents.name: Exercise 3.60: weakly sequentially closed set which is not weakly closed
contents.support: sqrt(n)e_n witness with square-summable finite tests and bounded sequences.

contents.name: Exercise 3.62: metrizable bounded dual ball
contents.support: Bounded metric belongs to the next owned pair.

contents.name: Exercise 3.22: Schur property
contents.reason: The full Schur theorem is assigned to the next pair; this pair only uses the explicit summation-functional obstruction.

contents.name: Exercise 3.23: weak metrizability under separable dual
contents.reason: This is bounded weak metrizability with a separable dual, needed in the later sequential compactness development.

contents.name: Exercise 3.24: canonical embedding and weak topology
contents.reason: The relative weak/weak-star embedding identification is a prerequisite argument of the next pair’s reflexive compactness theorem.

contents.name: Exercise 3.61: Schur and convex hulls in ell1
contents.reason: The Schur-dependent consequence follows the full Schur proof in the next pair, not this elementary weak-topology inventory.

contents.name: Corollary 3.28: weak-star closure of the dual sphere
contents.reason: The assigned sphere theorem concerns the primal weak topology; this distinct dual-sphere closure is not needed by a consumer in these pairs.

sources.title: Gerald Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis, 2017
sources.locator: §4.4 selected Lemma 4.28 and sequence examples pp125–128; §5.3 pp146–149 named results below.

contents.name: Lemma 4.28: elementary weak convergence properties
contents.support: Boundedness and norm lower semicontinuity; source uses uniform boundedness and does not certify the design’s choice refinement.

contents.name: Coordinate-vector examples in ellp and ell1
contents.support: Dual tests and constant ell-infinity functional; scalar convention must match local duality.

contents.name: Weak topologies and formula (5.12)
contents.support: Explicit series metric on bounded sets, not on the entire dual.

contents.name: Theorem 5.11: Mazur closure theorem
contents.support: Complex separation uses real parts.

contents.name: Example: weak closure of the unit sphere
contents.support: Finite-test kernel proof in infinite dimension.

contents.name: Theorem 5.13: Goldstine
contents.support: Finite-data separation proof and dual-norm contradiction.

contents.name: Theorem 4.29: weak convergence plus convergence of norms in Hilbert space
contents.reason: This is a geometric strengthening using Hilbert structure, outside the current elementary topology pair; it is retained for the later reflexive-space development.

contents.name: Theorem 4.30: reflexive subsequence extraction
contents.reason: Reflexive sequential compactness requires the subsequent Eberlein–Smulian and separability development.

contents.name: Corollary 5.12: norm approximation by convex combinations
contents.support: Apply equality of convex closures to the tails of a weakly convergent sequence.

contents.name: Theorem 3.30: Alaoglu in the separable case
contents.support: Replace the source’s diagonal selection with compact-metric tail closures and least admissible indices to avoid additional choice.

contents.name: Example 3.31: nonseparable dual ball without sequential compactness
contents.support: Coordinate evaluations on ell-infinity and alternating subsequence witness.

contents.name: Theorem 3.33: Alaoglu–Bourbaki
contents.support: Product embedding and closed linearity equations.

contents.name: Corollary 3.34: weak-star compact subsets of a Banach dual
contents.support: Closed bounded subsets are compact; converse boundedness uses uniform boundedness and completeness.

contents.name: Exercise 3.36: incomplete predual warning
contents.support: Adapt c00 and growing coordinate functionals; exact norm differs from the source and is checked directly.

contents.name: Exercise 3.37: compactness need not give a subsequence
contents.support: Nonseparable coordinate witness.

contents.name: Theorem 3.40: Banach–Dieudonné
contents.support: Full recursive finite-test proof and c0/ell1 separation route.

contents.name: Corollary 3.41: linear-subspace unit-ball criterion
contents.support: Scaling linear subspaces reduces bounded slices to the unit ball.

contents.name: Definition 3.45: extreme points and faces
contents.support: Faces include convexity; preserve distinction from exposed faces.

contents.name: Theorem 3.46: Krein–Milman
contents.support: Minimal compact face and separation, with Zorn/AC.

contents.name: Corollary 3.35: invariant compact sets
contents.reason: Invariant-set applications require a separate dynamical action and are not prerequisites for the compact convex geometry requested here.

contents.name: Exercise 3.38: ordinal sequential compactness without compactness
contents.reason: This is the converse topological failure on an ordinal space, not a dual-ball failure of sequential compactness.

contents.name: Exercise 3.39: point-mass embedding for locally compact spaces
contents.reason: The requested measure example is the compact-Hausdorff probability slice; the general locally compact embedding is a separate representation-topology application.

contents.name: Exercise 3.48: convex hull of an infinite simplex
contents.reason: This noncompact hull example is not used to assert compactness of arbitrary closed convex hulls; Milman explicitly assumes its closed convex hull is compact.

contents.name: Exercise 3.49: Hilbert cube
contents.reason: A Hilbert-cube worked example would require another compactness verification and is not needed for any of the seven assigned applications.

contents.name: Exercise 3.47: extreme boundary need not be compact
contents.reason: The suggested reflexive strictly convex example belongs with the later reflexive-space geometry; KM here never assumes the extreme boundary is compact.

contents.name: Theorem 5.8: extreme points in compact sets

contents.name: Theorem 5.9: Krein–Milman

contents.name: Examples: ell-infinity and c0 unit balls

contents.name: Theorem 5.10: Banach–Alaoglu
contents.support: Compact product route for bounded dual ball.

contents.name: Formula (5.12): weak-star metric

contents.name: Theorem 5.13: Goldstine
contents.support: Finite-dimensional separation with no compactness.

contents.name: Example: truncations in c0
contents.support: Concrete illustration of approximation inside a bidual ball.

contents.name: Example: extreme points of ell1 ball

contents.name: Lipschitz-ball extreme points example

sources.title: Ian Ball, Bauer’s Maximum Principle for Quasiconvex Functions
sources.locator: pp1–4: Theorem 1, standard convex proof on pp1–2, quasiconvex extension on pp3–4. Full six-page paper read.

contents.name: Standard proof for convex objectives
contents.support: Maximum set is compact and extremal; a minimal extremal subset is a singleton.

contents.name: Theorem 1: quasiconvex extension
contents.reason: The assigned Bauer theorem assumes convexity. Quasiconvexity is a strictly broader objective class requiring additional semiextremal-set machinery.
